knowledge_base.purpose: Provide detailed knowledge about CBT, CBT+, CI/CD integration, execution flow, architecture, testing strategy, and business value.

what_is_cbt.title: What is CBT?
what_is_cbt.definition: CBT (Continuous Build and Test) is an automated software integration and confidence testing framework that executes predefined tests whenever a software change is submitted. It validates that newly integrated software is functioning correctly before it is merged into the main development branch.
what_is_cbt.simple_explanation: Whenever a developer makes a code change, CBT automatically builds the software, downloads it to real hardware or simulated environments, executes a set of health and confidence tests, and reports the results. If tests pass, the software can proceed through the integration process. If tests fail, the change is rejected until issues are fixed.
business_goal: Prevent unstable software from entering mainline
what_is_cbt.key_message: Test every software change as early as possible.

what_is_cbt_plus.title: CBT+
what_is_cbt_plus.definition: CBT+ is an advanced version of CBT that extends traditional software confidence testing to software plus system confidence testing.

difference_from_cbt.CBT: Focuses mainly on software health checks and integration validations.
difference_from_cbt.CBT+: Validates both software behavior and actual system functionality using simulators, sensors, actuators and closed-loop environments.

benefits: Reduces dependency on expensive HIL environments

confidence_testing.definition: Confidence testing is a quick but meaningful validation process ensuring that previously working functionality continues to work after a software change.

non_regression_testing.definition: Ensures that new changes do not break existing functionality.

shift_left.definition: Move testing earlier in the development lifecycle so defects are discovered before becoming costly.

steps.name: Developer Check-In
steps.description: Developer submits code changes to source control repository.

steps.name: Build Trigger
steps.description: CI/CD system automatically triggers a software build.

steps.name: Integration Queue
steps.description: IQM (Integration Queue Manager) manages execution order and allocates available CBT benches.

steps.name: Software Flashing
steps.description: Generated software image is flashed into the target ECU.

steps.name: Automated Test Execution
steps.description: Confidence tests are executed automatically on dedicated CBT benches.

steps.name: Report Generation
steps.description: Detailed test reports are automatically generated.

steps.name: Quality Gate Decision
steps.description: Software is accepted only if mandatory tests pass.

steps.name: Mainline Integration
steps.description: Verified software is merged into the main branch.

ci_cd_integration.definition: CBT is a key component within the CI/CD pipeline.

layers.name: Variant Specific Layer
layers.purpose: Contains project-specific configuration, DBC, CDD, vehicle models, and security algorithms.

layers.name: Protocol Layer
layers.purpose: Contains UDS, GMLAN and communication services.

closed_loop_testing.definition: Testing where the ECU interacts with simulated or real-world feedback signals, creating a realistic operating environment.

faq.question: Why is CBT needed?
faq.answer: To automatically verify every software change and prevent unstable software from entering mainline.

faq.question: What is the difference between CBT and CBT+?
faq.answer: CBT focuses on software confidence testing while CBT+ validates both software and system behavior.

faq.question: Does CBT replace system testing?
faq.answer: No. CBT complements traditional SW/System testing and helps identify defects earlier.

faq.question: When does CBT execute?
faq.answer: Typically for every software change submitted to the integration pipeline.

faq.question: What happens if CBT fails?
faq.answer: The software change is blocked from integration until identified issues are resolved.

faq.question: What is confidence testing?
faq.answer: A fast validation approach used to ensure critical functionality still works after a software modification.

faq.question: What is Shift Left testing?
faq.answer: Testing earlier in the development lifecycle to reduce overall defect costs.
